title: MaxSup: Overcoming Representation Collapse in Label Smoothing

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 3.3 states: "L_LS ≈ α ( zgt − (1/K) ∑_{k=1}^K zk ) − log ∑_{j=1}^K e^{z_j}". The appendix (Section B) derives the exact equality L_LS = α (z_gt - (1/K)∑ z_k) without any extra -log∑ e^{z_j} term. The main text's expression is mathematically incorrect and contradicts the paper's own appendix proof.

The reference number [3] points to "Shiming Chen et al., HSVA: Hierarchical semantic-visual adaptation for zero-shot learning, NeurIPS 2021", which is unrelated to logit normalization. The correct paper (Wei et al., "Mitigating neural network overconfidence with logit normalization", 2022) is already listed as reference [38]. The citation [3*] is a misattribution.

Table 7 reports 'Low' (minority) class accuracy as exactly 0.0 for all methods (Focal Loss, LS, MaxSup) on CIFAR-10-LT with imbalance ratios 50 and 100, on both validation and test splits. The test set is balanced, so expecting zero accuracy across all methods is highly implausible and strongly suggests a bug in evaluation or a misreporting of results.

The paper states: "Further quantitative Grad-CAM overlay metrics (e.g., precision and recall for target regions) confirm that MaxSup yields more focused and comprehensive activation maps, further underscoring its overall efficacy." However, no such quantitative metrics are reported anywhere in the paper, making this claim unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1, rows '+ error amplification' with formulation α(z_gt - z_max)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Corollary 3.4 identifies the error amplification term as (α/K)∑_{z_n>z_gt}(z_gt - z_n). The table presents a different expression α(z_gt - z_max) and treats it as error amplification, which is not equivalent to the earlier decomposition. This inconsistency could mislead readers about what the error amplification term actually is.
